references.text: The Lord promises to drive out the nations before Israel, as also promised in Exodus 34:24.
The promise to expand Israel's borders is repeated here in Deuteronomy.
The command to appear before the face of the Lord three times a year is repeated, as in Exodus 34:24.
A parallel text that commands all men to appear before the Lord three times a year.
The Lord promises to drive out the peoples from the land before Israel.
The preceding verse containing the same command to appear before the Lord three times a year.
God's promise to Abraham to give his descendants the land and to drive out the nations.
The promise to expand Israel's territory when they keep God's commands.
The Lord drove out great and mighty nations before Israel.
No one shall covet (חמד) another's property—the same verb is used regarding not coveting the land.
The verses form a coherent theological explanation of how and why God's conquest of the land occurs gradually.
This verse presents the theological contrast to the promise in Exodus 34:24 by showing the consequence of breaking the covenant.
This verse serves as the theological warning against losing the land and security promised in Exodus 34:24.
